title: Errors and how to fix them
text: Every error below was reproduced against the current release. The exception type tells you which layer raised it: ChameleonRobynException comes from this package, while ValueError, NameError and KeyError come from Chameleon.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
section: You must call global_init() before rendering templates.
text:
You must call global_init() before rendering templates.
A template was rendered before the engine was initialized. Call global_init() at startup, before the first request. In tests this usually means a fixture called clear() and nothing re-initialized afterwards; see Testing your handlers.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
section: The specified template folder must be a folder, it's not: ...
text:
The specified template folder must be a folder, it's not: ...
The path passed to global_init() does not exist or is a file. Build it from __file__ rather than relying on the working directory:
template_folder = (Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'templates').as_posix()
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
section: Invalid return type <class '...'>, we expected a dict or Response as the return value.
text:
Invalid return type <class '...'>, we expected a dict or Response as the return value.
A decorated handler returned something other than a dict or a Robyn Response. Returning None by falling off the end of the function is the common cause, often after a not_found() call that was commented out. Return the model dict.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
text:
__response_callback__ must be callable, got <class '...'>.
The reserved key holds a value that is not a function. Pass the function itself, not the result of calling it: '__response_callback__': set_cookie, not set_cookie().
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
section: 'encoding' is reserved by Chameleon's render() and cannot be a template variable; rename the key.
text:
'encoding' is reserved by Chameleon's render() and cannot be a template variable; rename the key.
Chameleon’s render() takes encoding as a named parameter. Pick another name for that variable, such as charset or file_encoding.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
text:
ChameleonRobynNotFoundException escapes to Robyn
not_found() was called outside a @template-decorated handler, so nothing caught it. Either decorate the handler or return chameleon_robyn.response('errors/404.pt', status_code=404, message='...') instead.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
text:
ValueError naming a template file
The template does not exist under the template folder. Check these in order:

The path is relative to the folder you passed to global_init(), not to the current file.
With auto-naming, the expected file is <module>/<function>.html or <module>/<function>.pt, where <module> is the last segment of the handler’s module name. For a script run directly it is the script’s file name, so index() in app.py expects app/index.pt (with __main__/index.pt as a fallback).
A not_found() call expects errors/404.pt to exist unless you passed another template.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
text:
NameError: <name>
The template uses a variable the handler did not pass. Chameleon reports the expression, the file and the line. Add the key to the returned dict, or guard the expression in the template with tal:condition.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
text:
KeyError: ':class', KeyError: '@click' or similar
An Alpine.js, htmx or Vue-style attribute was parsed under Chameleon’s restricted namespace. Pass restricted_namespace=False to global_init() or to ChameleonTemplate. See Writing templates.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
section: A parse error naming a file and line
text:
A parse error naming a file and line
Chameleon templates must be well-formed. Unclosed tags, a stray < in text, or an attribute without quotes stop the parser. Fix the markup at the reported line. Write < for a literal less-than sign and & for an ampersand in text.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
section: Template edits do not show up
text:
Template edits do not show up
auto_reload is False, which is the default. Pass auto_reload=True in development. See Configuration.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
section: A second global_init() call changed nothing
text:
A second global_init() call changed nothing
cache_init defaults to True, so a call made while the engine is initialized is ignored. Pass cache_init=False or call clear() first.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
section: The 404 page came back as text/html from an XML handler
text:
The 404 page came back as text/html from an XML handler
By design. not_found() always renders with status 404 and text/html, regardless of the handler’s content_type and status_code. To return a 404 in another format, build it with response(..., status_code=404, content_type='application/xml') and return it.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Errors and how to fix them
section: A $ shows up wrong in the page
text:
A $ shows up wrong in the page
${ starts an expression. Write $${price} to output a dollar sign followed by the value.
crumbs: Errors and how to fix them

title: Writing templates
Friendly 404 pages
How it works
text:
The library is three small files in chameleon_robyn/. Everything else in the repository is tests, example apps and documentation.

The global loader
global_init() creates one Chameleon PageTemplateLoader for the template folder and stores it, together with the folder path, in module-level state. render() looks a template up in that loader by its relative path and calls Chameleon’s render() with the keyword arguments as the template’s variables. response() calls render() and wraps the string in a Robyn Response with the requested status and content type. clear() drops the stored loader so the next global_init() starts fresh.


The decorator
template() returns a wrapper for the handler. It chooses a synchronous or asynchronous wrapper by checking whether the handler is a coroutine function, so await happens where it should. Both wrappers do the same work:

Call the handler.
If the result is a Robyn Response, return it unchanged.
If it is a dict, copy it, pop __response_callback__, render the template, build the Response, and call the callback with it.
Otherwise raise ChameleonRobynException.

Both wrappers also catch ChameleonRobynNotFoundException, which not_found() raises, and render the template it carries with status 404.
The wrappers use functools.wraps, which keeps the original function’s name and signature visible. Robyn inspects the handler signature when a route is registered to decide which arguments to pass, so this is what keeps request and typed path parameters working through the decorator.


Lazy template names
When the template path is omitted, the wrapper derives <module>/<function> and checks for the .html file on the first request rather than at decoration time. Routes are often decorated at import, before global_init() has run and before the template folder is known. Once the folder is known the resolved name is cached, so the file check happens once per handler.


404 via an exception
not_found() is declared NoReturn. It raises rather than returns so a handler can call it from inside a nested condition without the surrounding code needing to return its result. The exception carries the template path and message, and the decorator turns it into a response. This is also why it only works inside decorated handlers.


No Jinja2 dependency
Robyn’s TemplateInterface lives in a module that imports Jinja2 at the top. Subclassing it would make Jinja2 a hard dependency of this package. Instead, ChameleonTemplate implements a local Protocol with the same render_template() method, marked runtime_checkable so isinstance() checks still work. Robyn only cares about the method, so the class is interchangeable with JinjaTemplate in practice.

title: FAQ
text:
Do I have to call global_init() before decorating routes?
No. Explicit template paths are only used at request time, and auto-named templates are resolved at the first request. Decorate routes at import and call global_init() from main() if you prefer.


Why does my second global_init() call do nothing?
cache_init defaults to True, which makes later calls no-ops while the engine is initialized. Pass cache_init=False, or call clear() first. See Configuration.


Can one handler render different templates?
Yes. Build the alternative with response('other.pt', ...) and return it. A returned Response passes through the decorator untouched. See Rendering outside handlers.


How do I return a 404 outside a decorated handler?
not_found() only works inside @template handlers. Elsewhere, return response('errors/404.pt', status_code=404, message='...'). See Friendly 404 pages.


Why did my 404 page come back as HTML from an XML endpoint?
not_found() always renders as text/html with status 404. For another format, build the response yourself with response().


How do I set a cookie on a rendered page?
Put a callable under the __response_callback__ key in the returned dict. It is called with the built Response. See the decorator guide.


Can I use .html files instead of .pt?
Yes. The loader ignores the extension. Auto-naming looks for .html first and then .pt.


My Alpine.js or htmx attributes break the template
Pass restricted_namespace=False to global_init(). See Writing templates.


Can Chameleon and Jinja2 templates coexist in one app?
Yes. Nothing in this package touches Robyn’s Jinja2 support. Use @template or ChameleonTemplate for Chameleon pages and Robyn’s JinjaTemplate for the rest.


Does it work with chameleon-partials?
Yes, with no extra configuration. Initialize both packages with the same template folder and pass render_partial through the model. See Writing templates.


How do I test a handler?
Call it directly and assert on the returned Response. No server needed. See Testing your handlers.


Is the API stable?
Not yet. The project is in alpha. The surface is small and the current names are expected to stay, but there are no guarantees until 1.0.


Where is the template language documented?
At chameleon.readthedocs.io. The cheat sheet covers the parts you need day to day.

SKILL.md
---
name: chameleon-robyn
description: Render Chameleon page templates (.pt files using TAL and METAL) from Robyn web handlers. A handler returns a dict and the @template decorator turns it into a Robyn Response. Use when adding Chameleon templates to a Robyn app, when a handler should return a dict that becomes an HTML page, when a ChameleonRobynException or a Chameleon ValueError, NameError or KeyError appears while rendering, when choosing between @template, response(), render() and ChameleonTemplate, when a 404 page or a cookie must be set on a rendered page, or when Alpine.js or htmx attributes fail to parse in a template.
license: MIT
compatibility: Requires Python >=3.10, robyn>=0.60 and Chameleon. No Jinja2 dependency.
---

# chameleon-robyn

Robyn ships with Jinja2. This package lets a Robyn handler return a plain `dict` and renders it through a Chameleon page template (`.pt`, TAL/METAL syntax, not Jinja syntax) into a `robyn.Response`. Errors from this package are `ChameleonRobynException`; errors about the template itself come from Chameleon (`ValueError` for a missing file, `NameError` for a missing variable, `KeyError` for a disallowed attribute).

## Install

```bash
uv pip install chameleon-robyn   # or: pip install chameleon-robyn
```

## Use

```python
from pathlib import Path
from robyn import Robyn
import chameleon_robyn

app = Robyn(__file__)

@app.get('/episodes/:episode_id')                 # Robyn route decorator outermost
@chameleon_robyn.template('episodes/detail.pt')  # @template directly above the function
async def episode_detail(request, episode_id: int):
    episode = await get_episode(episode_id)
    if not episode:
        chameleon_robyn.not_found()               # renders errors/404.pt, status 404
    return {'episode': episode}                   # the dict is the template model

def main():
    templates = (Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'templates').as_posix()
    chameleon_robyn.global_init(templates, auto_reload=True)  # once at startup; auto_reload for dev only
    app.start(host='127.0.0.1', port=8000)
```

Template `templates/episodes/detail.pt` (valid HTML; logic lives in `tal:` attributes, interpolation is `${...}`):

```html
<metal:block use-macro="load: ../shared/layout.pt">
<div metal:fill-slot="content">
  <h1>${episode.title}</h1>
  <li tal:repeat="g episode.guests">${g.name}</li>
  <p tal:condition="not episode.guests">No guests.</p>
</div>
</metal:block>
```

## Rules

- A decorated handler must return a `dict` or a `robyn.Response`. Anything else, including `None`, raises `ChameleonRobynException` at request time.
- A returned `Response` passes through untouched. That is how redirects work, and how a handler renders a different template: `return chameleon_robyn.response('other.pt', status_code=401, **model)`.
- All template paths are relative to the folder passed to `global_init()`. The default 404 template is `errors/404.pt`; create it in every app that calls `not_found()`.
- `global_init()` is one-shot by default. With `cache_init=True` (the default) a second call is silently ignored. Pass `cache_init=False` or call `clear()` first to change settings, including in test fixtures.
- Bare `@template` or `@template()` derives `<module>/<function>.html`, falling back to `<module>/<function>.pt`, where `<module>` is the last segment of the module name. For a script run directly (`python app.py`) it is the script's file stem, so `index()` in `app.py` expects `app/index.pt`, with `__main__/index.pt` as a legacy fallback. The name is resolved at the first request, so `global_init()` may run after the routes are decorated.
- `not_found()` only works inside `@template` handlers, because the decorator catches the exception it raises. The 404 always renders as `text/html` with status 404, ignoring the handler's `content_type` and `status_code`. Outside a decorated handler use `response('errors/404.pt', status_code=404, message='...')`.
- Raise `ChameleonRobynNotFoundException('your message')` directly to put a custom message into the 404 template; `not_found()` passes a fixed message as `message`.
- `__response_callback__` is a reserved model key. Its value must be callable (else `ChameleonRobynException`), it is popped from a copy of the dict before rendering, it never reaches the template, and it is called with the built `Response`. Mutate the response in place; the return value is ignored.
- `encoding` is a reserved model key. Chameleon's `render()` takes it as a parameter, so passing it raises `ChameleonRobynException`. Rename the variable.
- Chameleon's default restricted namespace rejects `@click`, `:class`, `x-on:click` and similar Alpine.js or htmx attributes with a `KeyError`. Pass `restricted_namespace=False` to `global_init()` or `ChameleonTemplate`.
- `${...}` output is HTML-escaped. Use `tal:replace="structure expr"` for pre-rendered HTML, including chameleon-partials output. A literal `$` before `{` is written `$${...}`.
- `ChameleonTemplate` has its own loader and ignores `global_init()`. Its `render_template()` always returns status 200 with `text/html`.
- Sync and async handlers both work; the wrapper is chosen automatically. `functools.wraps` preserves the signature, so Robyn still injects `request` and typed path params.
- Templates must be well-formed HTML/XML. There is no `{% %}` or `{ }` syntax.

## Decision table

| Need | Use |
|---|---|
| Render a template from a Robyn handler | `@chameleon_robyn.template('dir/page.pt')` and return a `dict` |
| Template named after the module and function | bare `@chameleon_robyn.template` |
| Non-200 status or non-HTML content type for a page | `@template('feed.xml', content_type='application/xml', status_code=200)` |
| Redirect from a decorated handler | return `robyn.Response(status_code=302, description='', headers=Headers({'Location': '/x'}))` |
| Render a different template in some branch | return `chameleon_robyn.response('other.pt', status_code=..., **model)` |
| Friendly 404 inside a decorated handler | `chameleon_robyn.not_found()` or `not_found(four04template_file='errors/custom.pt')` |
| 404 with a custom message | `raise ChameleonRobynNotFoundException('message')` |
| 404 or 500 outside a decorated handler | `chameleon_robyn.response('errors/404.pt', status_code=404, message='...')` |
| Set a cookie or header on a rendered page | `'__response_callback__': fn` in the dict; `fn(resp)` does `resp.headers.append('Set-Cookie', ...)` |
| HTML as a string (emails, fragments) | `chameleon_robyn.render('emails/welcome.pt', **model)` |
| Robyn's JinjaTemplate-style engine object | `ChameleonTemplate('templates/').render_template('page.pt', **model)` |
| Alpine.js or htmx attributes in templates | `global_init(..., restricted_namespace=False)` |
| Templates reload on edit | `global_init(..., auto_reload=True)` in development only |
| Re-initialize with new settings (tests) | `global_init(folder, cache_init=False)` and `clear()` in teardown |
| Reusable partials | chameleon-partials: `register_extensions(folder)` at startup, pass `render_partial` in the dict, insert with `tal:replace="structure render_partial('shared/card.pt', item=item)"` |

## API

- `global_init(template_folder: str, auto_reload=False, cache_init=True, restricted_namespace=True) -> None`. Raises `ChameleonRobynException` if the folder is empty or not a directory. No-op when already initialized unless `cache_init=False`.
- `clear() -> None`. Resets to uninitialized; rendering afterwards raises `ChameleonRobynException` until `global_init()` runs again.
- `template(template_file: str | None = None, content_type='text/html', status_code=200)`. Decorator; also usable bare. `charset=utf-8` is appended to the content type.
- `not_found(four04template_file='errors/404.pt') -> NoReturn`. Raises `ChameleonRobynNotFoundException(message, template)`.
- `render(template_file: str, **model) -> str`. Raises `ChameleonRobynException` if uninitialized or `encoding` is in the model; Chameleon raises `ValueError` if the file is missing.
- `response(template_file: str, content_type='text/html', status_code=200, **model) -> robyn.Response`. Same errors as `render()`.
- `ChameleonTemplate(directory: str, auto_reload=False, encoding='utf-8', restricted_namespace=True)` with `.render_template(template_name: str, **model) -> robyn.Response` (always 200, `text/html`).
- `ChameleonRobynException(Exception)`: base for every error this package raises.
- `ChameleonRobynNotFoundException(message=None, four04template_file='errors/404.pt')`: subclass carrying `.message` and `.template_file`.

## Reading an error

```text
chameleon_robyn.exceptions.ChameleonRobynException: Invalid return type <class 'NoneType'>, we expected a dict or Response as the return value.
```

The handler fell off the end without returning the dict, usually after a `not_found()` call was removed. Fix order for rendering problems: initialize (`global_init()` ran, folder exists), then path (relative to the folder, auto-name matches `<module>/<function>`), then model (every `${name}` in the template is a key in the dict), then markup (well-formed, `restricted_namespace` if using Alpine/htmx).

## Resources

- Docs: <https://mkennedy.codes/docs/chameleon-robyn/>
- Decorator guide: <https://mkennedy.codes/docs/chameleon-robyn/user-guide/template-decorator.html>
- Writing templates (TAL cheat sheet, METAL, partials): <https://mkennedy.codes/docs/chameleon-robyn/user-guide/templates.html>
- Errors and fixes: <https://mkennedy.codes/docs/chameleon-robyn/user-guide/troubleshooting.html>
- Testing handlers: <https://mkennedy.codes/docs/chameleon-robyn/user-guide/testing.html>
- API index: <https://mkennedy.codes/docs/chameleon-robyn/llms.txt>
- Full docs for agents: <https://mkennedy.codes/docs/chameleon-robyn/llms-full.txt>
- Every docs page is also served as Markdown by swapping `.html` for `.md`, for example <https://mkennedy.codes/docs/chameleon-robyn/reference/template.md>

title: response()
text:
Render a Chameleon template and wrap it in a fully-formed Robyn Response.


Usage
Source


response(
    template_file, content_type="text/html", status_code=200, **template_data
)


Useful where the @template decorator does not fit: error handlers, middleware, or a handler that renders different templates depending on the request.


Parameters


template_file: str

The template file path, relative to the template folder.

content_type: str = "text/html"

The Content-Type header value (defaults to text/html).

status_code: int = 200

The HTTP status code for the response (defaults to 200).

**template_data: Any

Values passed to the template as its model.





Returns


 Response

A Robyn Response with the rendered template as its body.





Raises


 ChameleonRobynException

If global_init() has not been called, or the model uses the reserved key ‘encoding’.





Examples
resp = chameleon_robyn.response('errors/500.pt', status_code=500, error=str(e))

title: not_found()
text:
Render a friendly 404 page from within a @template-decorated handler.


Usage
Source


not_found(four04template_file="errors/404.pt")


Raises an exception that the @template decorator catches and converts into a 404 response rendered through the given template. The template receives a message variable describing the 404. Only works inside handlers decorated with @template.


Parameters


four04template_file: str = "errors/404.pt"

The template to render, relative to the template folder (defaults to ‘errors/404.pt’).





Raises


 ChameleonRobynNotFoundException

Always; carries the 404 template path.





Examples
@app.get('/episodes/:episode_id')
@chameleon_robyn.template('episodes/detail.pt')
def episode_detail(request, episode_id: int):
    episode = get_episode(episode_id)
    if not episode:
        chameleon_robyn.not_found()  # renders errors/404.pt with status 404
    return {'episode': episode}

title: global_init()
text:
Initialize the Chameleon template engine.


Usage
Source


global_init(
    template_folder,
    auto_reload=False,
    cache_init=True,
    restricted_namespace=True
)


Call this once at startup, before the first request is rendered. Routes may be decorated with @template before this runs; auto-named templates are resolved lazily at the first request.


Parameters


template_folder: str

Path to the template directory. All template paths passed to @template, render(), response() and not_found() are relative to this folder.

auto_reload: bool = False

Whether to re-read templates when they change on disk. Use True in development only; it disables caching.

cache_init: bool = True

If True (the default) and the engine is already initialized, the call is ignored and the earlier settings stay in effect. Pass False to re-initialize with new settings (tests do this), or call clear() first.

restricted_namespace: bool = True

If True, only TAL/METAL/i18n namespaces are allowed in attributes. If False, attribute-based JS frameworks like Alpine.js and htmx can use shorthand syntax (@click, :class, etc.).





Raises


 ChameleonRobynException

If template_folder is empty or is not an existing directory.





Examples
from pathlib import Path
import chameleon_robyn

templates = (Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'templates').as_posix()
chameleon_robyn.global_init(templates, auto_reload=True)  # auto_reload for development only

title: ChameleonTemplate
text: Chameleon template engine implementing Robyn’s TemplateInterface.

title: ChameleonTemplate
text:
render_template()

Render a template and return a 200 Robyn Response.


Usage
Source


render_template(template_name, **kwargs)


Parameters


template_name: str

The template file path, relative to the directory given at construction.

**kwargs: Any

Values passed to the template as its model. The key ‘encoding’ is reserved.





Returns


 Response

A Robyn Response with the rendered template as its body. The status is always 200
and the Content-Type is always text/html.





Raises


 ChameleonRobynException

If the model uses the reserved key ‘encoding’.

title: ChameleonRobynException
text:
Base exception for all chameleon-robyn errors (bad configuration, invalid return types, etc.).


Usage
Source


ChameleonRobynException()


Examples
try:
    chameleon_robyn.render('home/index.pt', title='Home')
except chameleon_robyn.ChameleonRobynException as e:
    log.error('template setup problem: %s', e)

title: chameleon-robyn
chameleon-robyn
chameleon-robyn
chameleon-robyn
text:
Lower-level API
Sometimes you need to render a template outside of a decorator - in middleware, error handlers, or helper functions.

render() - get an HTML string
html = chameleon_robyn.render('emails/welcome.pt', username='Michael')
# Returns a string, no Response wrapping


response() - get a Robyn Response
resp = chameleon_robyn.response('errors/500.pt', status_code=500, error=str(e))
# Returns a fully-formed Robyn Response object
One reserved name: a template variable called encoding cannot be passed, because Chameleon’s own render() takes it as a parameter. The library raises ChameleonRobynException if you try. More in rendering outside handlers.

title: chameleon-robyn
chameleon-robyn
text:
global_init() reference
chameleon_robyn.global_init(
    template_folder,              # Path to your templates directory (required)
    auto_reload=False,            # Watch for template changes - use True in development
    cache_init=True,              # Skip re-initialization if already called
    restricted_namespace=True,    # Set to False if using Alpine.js, htmx @attributes, etc.
)

Alpine.js / htmx compatibility
Chameleon’s default namespace rules reject attributes like @click or :class because they look like XML namespace prefixes. If you’re using Alpine.js, htmx, or similar libraries, set restricted_namespace=False:
chameleon_robyn.global_init(template_folder, restricted_namespace=False)
This tells Chameleon to allow any attribute syntax in your templates. Every global_init() setting is described in configuration.

chameleon-robyn
text:
Example apps
The repo includes two example apps you can run to see everything in action.

Setup
Clone the repo and install with the extras you need:
git clone https://github.com/mikeckennedy/chameleon-robyn.git
cd chameleon-robyn
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate      # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# Install the package with example dependencies
pip install -e ".[examples]"


example/ - Core features
A Robyn app demonstrating the @template decorator, sync and async handlers, METAL macro layout inheritance, response pass-through redirects, a __response_callback__ cookie example, friendly 404 pages, search with query parameters, and an XML feed with a custom content type.
python example/app.py
# Open http://127.0.0.1:5555


example-partials/ - With chameleon-partials
The same app, but refactored to use chameleon-partials for reusable template components. The episode card markup lives in a single shared/episode_card.pt partial that’s shared across the episodes list and search results pages.
python example-partials/app.py
# Open http://127.0.0.1:5555
Compare the two to see how partials reduce template duplication - the episode list and search results templates go from inline card markup to a single tal:replace call each.

title: ChameleonRobynNotFoundException
text:
Raised by not_found() to signal a 404 from within a @template-decorated handler.


Usage
Source


ChameleonRobynNotFoundException(
    message=None, four04template_file="errors/404.pt"
)


The @template decorator catches this exception and renders the template it carries with a 404 status code, passing the message to the template as message.


Parameters


message: Optional[str] = None

Optional human-readable description of the 404.

four04template_file: str = "errors/404.pt"

The 404 template to render, relative to the template folder.





Examples
Raise it directly to supply your own message to the 404 template:
raise ChameleonRobynNotFoundException(f'No episode with id {episode_id}.')

title: clear()
text:
Reset the template engine to its uninitialized state.


Usage
Source


clear()


After calling this, global_init() must be called again before rendering. Mostly useful in tests to isolate template configuration between cases.


Examples
import pytest
import chameleon_robyn

@pytest.fixture
def templates(tmp_path):
    chameleon_robyn.global_init(str(tmp_path), cache_init=False)
    yield
    chameleon_robyn.clear()

title: API Reference
text:
Everything chameleon-robyn exports: setup, the @template decorator, lower-level rendering, and the Robyn TemplateInterface implementation.


Setup & configuration

Initialize the template engine once at app startup.


global_init()

Initialize the Chameleon template engine.

clear()

Reset the template engine to its uninitialized state.




Rendering views

The @template decorator and friendly 404s for Robyn route handlers.


template()

Decorate a Robyn view method to render an HTML response.

not_found()

Render a friendly 404 page from within a @template-decorated handler.




Lower-level rendering

Render templates outside the decorator (middleware, error handlers, emails).


render()

Render a Chameleon template to a string (no Response wrapping).

response()

Render a Chameleon template and wrap it in a fully-formed Robyn Response.




Robyn TemplateInterface

Standalone template engine class matching Robyn’s built-in template pattern.


ChameleonTemplate

Chameleon template engine implementing Robyn’s TemplateInterface.




Exceptions

Exception types raised by the library.


ChameleonRobynException

Base exception for all chameleon-robyn errors (bad configuration, invalid return types, etc.).

ChameleonRobynNotFoundException

Raised by not_found() to signal a 404 from within a @template-decorated handler.

title: render()
text:
Render a Chameleon template to a string (no Response wrapping).


Usage
Source


render(template_file, **template_data)


Useful outside of route handlers: emails, middleware, error handlers, etc.


Parameters


template_file: str

The template file path, relative to the template folder (e.g. ‘emails/welcome.pt’).

**template_data: Any

Values passed to the template as its model. The key ‘encoding’ is reserved by Chameleon and cannot be used.





Returns


 str

The rendered template as a string.





Raises


 ChameleonRobynException

If global_init() has not been called, or the model uses the reserved key ‘encoding’.

 ValueError

Raised by Chameleon when the template file does not exist.





Examples
html = chameleon_robyn.render('emails/welcome.pt', username='Michael')

title: template()
text:
Decorate a Robyn view method to render an HTML response.


Usage
Source


template(template_file=None, content_type="text/html", status_code=200)


The decorated handler returns a dict (the template model). If the template path is omitted, it is derived from the module and function name: module/function.html if that file exists, otherwise module/function.pt. For a script run directly (module main) the script’s file name is used instead, so index() in app.py maps to app/index.pt; a legacy main/function.html or .pt is still found if the script-named file does not exist. The auto-derived name is resolved at first request, so global_init() may be called after route decoration. Handlers that return a Robyn Response are passed through untouched (redirects, custom errors). Works with sync and async handlers.
Place @template directly above the handler, below Robyn’s route decorator.


Parameters


template_file: Optional[Union[Callable, str]] = None

Optional, the Chameleon template file (path relative to template folder, *.pt).

content_type: str = "text/html"

The Content-Type header value for rendered responses (defaults to text/html).

status_code: int = 200

The HTTP status code for rendered responses (defaults to 200).





Returns


 Callable

Decorator for Robyn route handlers.





Raises


 ChameleonRobynException

At request time, if the handler returns something other than a dict or a Robyn Response, or if ‘response_callback’ is not callable.





Examples
@app.get('/episodes/:episode_id')
@chameleon_robyn.template('episodes/detail.pt')
async def episode_detail(request, episode_id: int):
    return {'episode': await get_episode(episode_id)}

@app.get('/')
@chameleon_robyn.template  # renders <module>/index.html or <module>/index.pt
def index(request):
    return {'title': 'Home'}

title: Configuration
text:
All configuration is one function call at startup. There are no environment variables and no config files.
chameleon_robyn.global_init(
    template_folder,              # required
    auto_reload=False,
    cache_init=True,
    restricted_namespace=True,
)








Parameter
Default
What it does




template_folder
required
Path to the directory holding your templates. Must exist, or ChameleonRobynException is raised. Every template path elsewhere in the API is relative to it.


auto_reload
False
When True, Chameleon re-reads a template when the file changes on disk. Use it in development. Leave it off in production so compiled templates stay cached.


cache_init
True
When True and the engine is already initialized, the call does nothing and the earlier settings stay in effect. Pass False to re-initialize with new settings.


restricted_namespace
True
When True, only the tal:, metal: and i18n: attribute namespaces are allowed. Set it to False for Alpine.js, htmx and other libraries that use @click, :class or similar attributes.




Where to call it
Either place works:

At import time, before the routes, as in the getting started example.
From main() right before app.start(), after the routes have been decorated. Auto-named templates are resolved at the first request, so this is fine, and it is the pattern the example apps use.

Build the path from __file__ so it does not depend on the working directory:
from pathlib import Path

def main():
    dev_mode = True
    template_folder = (Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'templates').as_posix()
    chameleon_robyn.global_init(template_folder, auto_reload=dev_mode)
    app.start(host='127.0.0.1', port=5555)


Calling it twice
With the default cache_init=True, a second call is ignored. This is deliberate: a module that calls global_init() on import cannot clobber the settings the app chose. It also means changing a setting at runtime requires either cache_init=False or a clear() first:
chameleon_robyn.clear()
chameleon_robyn.global_init(other_folder, restricted_namespace=False)
clear() resets the engine to its uninitialized state. Rendering after clear() and before the next global_init() raises ChameleonRobynException. Its main use is in tests; see Testing your handlers.


Development versus production









Development
Production




auto_reload
True, so template edits show up on the next request
False, so each template is compiled once and cached


restricted_namespace
False if you use Alpine.js or htmx attributes, otherwise leave the default
same as development



A dev_mode flag driven by your own settings is the usual way to switch, as in the example above.

title: Getting started
text:
Robyn ships with Jinja2 templating. chameleon-robyn lets you use Chameleon page templates instead: .pt files that are valid HTML, with tal: attributes for logic and METAL macros for shared layouts. If you have used Chameleon with Pyramid, Flask, or FastAPI, the templates are the same. The package adds a @template decorator so a Robyn handler returns a plain dict and the caller gets back a rendered Robyn Response.
The project is in alpha. The API is small and unlikely to change much, but there are no stability promises yet.

Install
uv pip install chameleon-robyn
Or with pip:
pip install chameleon-robyn
This installs robyn and chameleon as dependencies. Python 3.10 or newer is required.


Project layout
my_app/
├── app.py
└── templates/
    └── home/
        └── index.pt
Every template path you give the library is relative to the templates/ folder you register at startup. The folder name itself is up to you.


Your first page
Create templates/home/index.pt:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<body>
    <h1>Hello, ${name}!</h1>
    <ul>
        <li tal:repeat="item items">${item}</li>
    </ul>
</body>
</html>
Create app.py:
from pathlib import Path
from robyn import Robyn
import chameleon_robyn

app = Robyn(__file__)

# Point Chameleon at your templates folder (do this once at startup)
template_folder = (Path(__file__).resolve().parent / 'templates').as_posix()
chameleon_robyn.global_init(template_folder, auto_reload=True)

@app.get('/')
@chameleon_robyn.template('home/index.pt')
async def index(request):
    return {'name': 'World', 'items': ['Robyn', 'Chameleon', 'Python']}

app.start(host='127.0.0.1', port=8000)
Run python app.py and open http://127.0.0.1:8000/. You should see the heading and a three-item list.


What just happened

global_init() told Chameleon where the templates live. It runs once at startup. The settings are covered in Configuration.
@template('home/index.pt') wrapped the handler. The handler returned a dict, and every key in it became a variable in the template.
The decorator rendered the template and returned a Robyn Response with status 200 and a Content-Type of text/html; charset=utf-8.
Robyn’s route decorator stayed on the outside. @template goes directly above the function, and it works for both def and async def handlers.



Example apps
The repository has two runnable apps that show every feature: episodes and guests pages, a shared METAL layout, a search page using query parameters, an XML feed, a redirect, a cookie set from a rendered page, and a friendly 404.
git clone https://github.com/mikeckennedy/chameleon-robyn.git
cd chameleon-robyn
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate      # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -e ".[examples]"

python example/app.py           # core features
python example-partials/app.py  # the same app using chameleon-partials
# Open http://127.0.0.1:5555


Where to go next

The @template decorator: explicit and auto-named templates, async handlers, status codes, redirects, and setting cookies on a rendered page.
Writing templates: a TAL cheat sheet, METAL layouts, escaping, Alpine.js and htmx attributes, and chameleon-partials.
Friendly 404 pages: not_found() and custom 404 templates.
Rendering outside handlers: render(), response(), and the standalone ChameleonTemplate class.
Configuration: every global_init() setting, and development versus production.
Testing your handlers: call decorated handlers directly, without starting a server.
Errors and how to fix them: what each exception means and what to change.
How it works: the three source files and the design choices behind them.
FAQ
API reference

title: Rendering outside handlers
text:
The decorator covers route handlers. Three other entry points cover everything else: middleware, error handlers, email bodies, and apps that prefer Robyn’s built-in template-engine pattern.

render(): get a string
html = chameleon_robyn.render('emails/welcome.pt', username='Michael')
Returns the rendered template as a str. Keyword arguments are the template variables. It requires global_init() to have been called and raises ChameleonRobynException otherwise.


response(): get a Robyn Response
resp = chameleon_robyn.response('errors/500.pt', status_code=500, error=str(e))
Renders the template and wraps it in a Response with the given status (default 200) and content type (default text/html, with charset=utf-8 appended). The remaining keyword arguments are the template variables.
Because @template passes a returned Response through untouched, response() is also how a decorated handler renders a different template than the one in the decorator:
@app.post('/account/login')
@chameleon_robyn.template('account/welcome.pt')
async def login(request):
    user = await authenticate(request)
    if not user:
        return chameleon_robyn.response('account/login_failed.pt', status_code=401)
    return {'user': user}


A reserved variable name
Chameleon’s own render() takes the output encoding as a named parameter, so a template variable called encoding cannot be passed. The library raises ChameleonRobynException with a clear message if you try. Rename the key.


ChameleonTemplate: Robyn’s TemplateInterface pattern
Robyn’s own templating module exposes a JinjaTemplate class with a render_template() method. ChameleonTemplate has the same shape:
from chameleon_robyn import ChameleonTemplate

chameleon = ChameleonTemplate('templates/', auto_reload=True)

@app.get('/page')
def page(request):
    return chameleon.render_template('page.pt', title='Hello')
Points to know:

It owns its own template loader and does not use or require global_init(). You can mix it with the decorator API in one app, but each has its own folder setting.
render_template() always returns status 200 with text/html. For other statuses use response().
The constructor takes directory, auto_reload, encoding and restricted_namespace. See the reference.
It matches Robyn’s TemplateInterface through a structural Protocol rather than by subclassing Robyn’s abstract class. Importing Robyn’s class would import Jinja2, and this package deliberately has no Jinja2 dependency.

title: The @template decorator
Testing your handlers
text:
You do not need a running Robyn server to test a decorated handler. The decorator returns an ordinary function (or coroutine function) that returns a Robyn Response, so call it directly and assert on the result. This is how the package’s own test suite works.

Point the engine at test templates
Use a fixture that initializes the engine with cache_init=False, so each test gets the folder it asks for, and clears it afterwards:
# conftest.py
from pathlib import Path
import pytest
import chameleon_robyn

@pytest.fixture
def templates():
    folder = Path(__file__).parent / 'templates'
    chameleon_robyn.global_init(str(folder), cache_init=False)
    yield
    chameleon_robyn.clear()
Without cache_init=False, the first global_init() in the test session would win and later fixtures would silently keep its settings.


Call the handler
from robyn import Response
import chameleon_robyn

def test_index_renders(templates):
    @chameleon_robyn.template('home/index.pt')
    def index(request):
        return {'name': 'World', 'items': ['a', 'b']}

    resp = index(None)
    assert isinstance(resp, Response)
    assert resp.status_code == 200
    assert 'Hello, World!' in resp.description
    assert 'text/html' in resp.headers.get('content-type')
The rendered HTML is in resp.description. Headers are a Robyn Headers object with get().
Handlers usually take a request argument. Pass None or a simple stand-in when the handler does not use it, or test the handler’s logic through a helper function that the handler calls.


Async handlers
Run the coroutine to completion:
import asyncio

def test_async_detail(templates):
    @chameleon_robyn.template('episodes/detail.pt')
    async def detail(request, episode_id: int):
        return {'episode': {'id': episode_id, 'title': 'Test'}}

    resp = asyncio.run(detail(None, 7))
    assert resp.status_code == 200


Testing a 404
def test_missing_episode_is_404(templates):
    @chameleon_robyn.template('episodes/detail.pt')
    def detail(request, episode_id: int):
        chameleon_robyn.not_found()

    resp = detail(None, 999)
    assert resp.status_code == 404
    assert 'not found' in resp.description.lower()


Testing the response callback
The callback receives the built Response, so capture it:
def test_login_sets_cookie(templates):
    @chameleon_robyn.template('account/welcome.pt')
    def login(request):
        def set_cookie(resp):
            resp.headers.append('Set-Cookie', 'session=abc; Path=/')
        return {'user': 'michael', '__response_callback__': set_cookie}

    resp = login(None)
    assert resp.headers.get('set-cookie') == 'session=abc; Path=/'


Testing templates on their own
render() returns the HTML as a string, which keeps assertions about markup separate from handler logic:
def test_episode_card_shows_title(templates):
    html = chameleon_robyn.render('shared/episode_card.pt', ep={'title': 'Async All the Things'})
    assert 'Async All the Things' in html


What not to test
Chameleon’s own behaviour, such as escaping, tal:repeat ordering, or error messages, is covered by Chameleon’s test suite. Test what your handlers return and what your templates show.
